gumtree_entries.description: UPDATED o2 -> i2: Basic unit tests for the alternative ByteArrayInputStream implementation.
ADDED i3: Reusable 3-byte data sequence used across multiple read/skip/mark tests.
ADDED i4: Convenience alias to avoid repeating the long field reference in assertions.
ADDED i6: Empty buffer: offset 0 => 0 bytes available; any positive offset => still 0
ADDED i7: Single-byte buffer: offset past the end clamps available to 0
ADDED i8: 25-byte buffer: available = bufferLength - offset (clamped to 0 when offset >= length)
ADDED i10: Empty buffer: available is always 0 regardless of offset/length
ADDED i11: Single-byte buffer: available = min(length, bufferSize - offset), floored at 0
ADDED i12: 25-byte buffer with various offset/length combinations
ADDED i13: Requested length exceeding actual buffer size is clamped to the remaining bytes
ADDED i20: Mark after reading the first byte; subsequent reads advance past the mark
ADDED i21: reset() repositions to the marked offset, allowing the same bytes to be re-read
ADDED i22: reset() can be called again to go back to the same mark a second time
ADDED i23: Reading from an empty stream returns END_OF_STREAM and leaves the buffer untouched
ADDED i24: A zero-length destination buffer causes read() to return 0 without consuming data
ADDED i25: Buffer larger than stream: all stream bytes are read; remaining buffer slots stay zero
ADDED i26: Buffer smaller than stream: first call fills the buffer, second call reads the remainder
ADDED i27: Empty stream always returns END_OF_STREAM regardless of the requested region
ADDED i28: len=0 always returns 0 without consuming any bytes
ADDED i29: Partial read of 2 bytes followed by a read that retrieves the single remaining byte
ADDED i30: Empty stream immediately signals end-of-stream
ADDED i31: Each successive call returns the next byte until the stream is exhausted
ADDED i32: Skip 1 leaves 2 bytes; next read returns the second byte
ADDED i33: skip(0) is a no-op: position and available count are unchanged
ADDED i34: Skip 2 leaves only the last byte readable
ADDED i35: Skipping exactly the stream length exhausts it without error
ADDED i36: Skipping more than available clamps to the end of the stream
